 Congress' expected richest member plans to target politicians who get rich in office
 Sunday, 15 November 2026, 17:11 
 Photo source: Fox News 
 Joe Strada says he plans to make politicians’ personal enrichment a target when he enters Congress in January, arguing that public office should be about serving Americans. 
 According to Forbes, Strada is expected to become Congress' richest member. He went from working as a bowling alley mechanic to owning a nationwide HVAC company.
 This is reported by Fox News .
 The incoming Republican said combating congressional insider trading and political profiteering would be among his priorities as he prepares to leave the private sector for Capitol Hill.
 Nobody, and I mean nobody, should get rich in public office. We're there to serve the American people. 
 - Joe Strada
 Strada cited his rise from a blue-collar worker to a successful businessman as evidence that the American Dream remains achievable. He argued that excessive government intervention has made it harder for others to follow a similar path.
 I started with nothing. I was a handyman at a bowling alley. If I can do it, other everyday Americans can. Government needs to get out of their way and help them succeed, 
 - Joe Strada
 He warned that the growing popularity of democratic socialism and proposals to expand government programs could undermine American entrepreneurship, innovation and small-business growth. Strada said his early work experience taught him discipline and perseverance, which he believes should be emphasized to younger generations.
 I think if we can instill that in young people today, they'd be better off. 
 - Joe Strada
 Strada also identified housing affordability as a major obstacle to financial independence. He pledged to pursue federal deregulation, lower construction material costs and workforce development initiatives to make homeownership more accessible.
 Housing cost is ridiculous. I have so many examples of ways we can still build a high-quality home for substantially less money, and more Americans could live out their dream of owning a home, 
 - Joe Strada
